changed.schema_words: +input.cik description: SEC Central Index Key. Give this or ticker.
changed.words: +When to use: You want one overview of a US public company: who it is, recent filings and headline numbers. Use instead: company_due_diligence for growth, margins, leverage and 8-K summaries; sec_company or sec_financials for just one part (cheaper). Parameters: ticker or cik (one is required). filings: how many recent filings, 1-40, default 8. form: only this form type. Returns: profile, filings[] with links, and key financials for the last two fiscal years and the latest quarter.

+When to use: You have 2-5 product page URLs, the same item at different stores or a short list. Use instead: get_product_details for a single URL. Returns: one entry per URL in order, each ok or with its error.

+When to use: You want the state of the crypto market in one call, for example before deciding anything else. Use instead: perps_market for specific coins or more markets; crypto_news for the headlines behind a move. Returns: Fear & Greed (today, yesterday, a week ago), BTC, ETH and SOL with perp price, 24h change, funding and Chainlink price, funding extremes, top gainers and losers, and Hyperliquid totals. Takes no parameters.

+When to use: You want what's being said about a coin or the market right now. Use instead: web_search with type "news" for non-crypto topics; crypto_market_pulse for numbers instead of headlines. Parameters: query: a coin or topic; leave it out for the whole market. freshness: hour, day (default) or week. num: 1-10 articles, default 8. Returns: articles[] with title, publisher, date, snippet and link, plus mood (positive, negative, mixed or neutral), a summary and themes, written only from those headlines.

changed.schema_words: +input.amount description: Amount to convert (default 1).
changed.words: +When to use: You need to convert between currencies at an official reference rate. Parameters: from and to: 3-letter codes (30 supported). amount: default 1. date: YYYY-MM-DD within the last 90 days; leave out for the latest business day. Returns: the rate, the converted amount and the ECB date used. For information, not for transactions.

+When to use: You need a paid API for a job and don't know which seller has it. Free. Use instead: best_x402_tools for a ranking by real repeat buyers; check_service when you already have the URL. Parameters: query: the job in plain words. limit: how many to check live, default 5. Returns: matching services, each checked live: whether it answered with a price, the price, network, recipient and paying wallets.

+When to use: You have a US street address and need its coordinates or census details. Use instead: weather_forecast takes the address directly if the weather is all you need. Parameters: address: a US street address with a house number. Returns: latitude and longitude, standardized address, ZIP, county, FIPS code, state and census tract. No match is refused free.

+When to use: You have the URL of one product page. Use instead: compare_products for 2-5 URLs (one payment); try_it_free to see the output first. Returns: product (name, price, currency, availability, brand, sku, images, variants), provenance of each field, and the page fetched.

+When to use: You want this service's prices, network and endpoints in machine-readable form. Free. Use instead: try_it_free to see real output. Returns: prices per tool, the payment network and recipient, and what each tool returns.

+When to use: You need roughly where an IP address is. Parameters: ip: one IPv4 or IPv6 address. Private and reserved addresses are refused free. Returns: country, region, city, continent and approximate latitude/longitude (city level, not a street address).

+When to use: You need the gist of one page, not its full text. Use instead: read_page for the full text; read_pages for several pages. Parameters: url: absolute https URL. max_words: summary length, 10-250, default 60. Returns: summary, title, final_url, and a note when the page was longer than the part summarized.

+When to use: The link is a PDF (a filing, paper, contract or manual) and you need its text. Use instead: read_page for an ordinary web page. Parameters: url: absolute http(s) URL of the PDF. max_pages: read at most this many pages, 1-300, default 50. Returns: title, author, page_count, pages_read and pages[] of text in order. Scanned PDFs with no text layer are refused at no charge.

+When to use: You need perpetual futures data from Hyperliquid: funding, open interest, leverage, or the top markets. Use instead: crypto_market_pulse for a one-call market overview; token_price for an on-chain spot price. Parameters: coins: up to 20 Hyperliquid names (e.g. BTC, ETH, kPEPE); leave out for the top markets. sort and limit (default volume, 10) apply only when coins is left out. funding_hours (1-168) adds hourly funding history and needs exactly one coin. Returns: markets[] with mark, oracle and mid price, 24h change, hourly and annualized funding (positive: longs pay shorts), ope

+When to use: Right before a trade, to see if the size is sane for the pool and what's being said about the token. Use instead: token_check when you aren't trading yet. Parameters: token is required. chain: base (default), ethereum or solana. amount_usd: your planned size, for price impact against pool depth. wallet: your address, to show what you already hold. Returns: price, liquidity, chain warnings, rough price impact for amount_usd, your current holding, and recent web results. Facts, not advice.

+When to use: You need past prices for a major asset: a trend, a high or low, or the change over a period. Use instead: token_price for the current price of any token, including ones without a Chainlink feed. Parameters: asset: a symbol with a Chainlink USD feed (ETH, BTC, SOL, LINK and others). days: 1-365, default 7. points: 2-100 evenly spaced prices, default 24. Returns: points[] each with time, price_usd and Chainlink round, plus first, last, high, low and percent change.

+When to use: You have one page URL and need its words: an article, doc, policy or listing. Use instead: read_pages for 2-5 URLs (one payment); page_brief for a summary instead of the full text; pdf_to_text for a PDF; screenshot_page for how it looks; attest_page if you may need to prove what it said. Parameters: url must be absolute http(s) and public (no logins, no private addresses). Returns: title, final_url after redirects, text (visible text, up to 50,000 characters), text_length and truncated.

+When to use: You picked 2-5 pages to read, for example from web_search results. Use instead: read_page for a single URL; search_and_read when you have a question but no URLs yet. Parameters: urls: 1-5 absolute http(s) URLs. Each is read in parallel; a page that fails doesn't stop the others. Returns: pages[] in the order given, each with ok, title, final_url, text (up to 20,000 characters) or the reason it failed; pages_read and pages_failed. Charged only if at least one page is read.

+When to use: You need to see a page: its layout, whether something renders, or an image for a vision model. Use instead: read_page when you only need the words (smaller and cheaper); attest_page for signed evidence of a page. Parameters: url must be absolute http(s) and public. Returns: a 1280x800 JPEG as base64, its sha256, title and final_url.

+When to use: Before buying, accepting or sending an unfamiliar token. Use instead: pretrade_check when you're about to trade a specific amount (adds price impact, your holding and news); token_info for the basics only. Parameters: token: ERC-20 contract or SPL mint. chain: base (default), ethereum or solana. Returns: what the token is, price and liquidity, and plain-language warnings (owner, upgradeable, can mint, pause, blacklist or set fees; Solana mint or freeze authority).

+When to use: You have a token address and need to know what it is before acting on it. Use instead: token_check for safety warnings and liquidity; token_price for its price. Parameters: token: ERC-20 contract or SPL mint. chain: base (default), ethereum or solana. Returns: name, symbol, decimals, total supply; on Solana, mint and freeze authority.

+When to use: You need a token's current USD price straight from the chain. Use instead: price_history for past prices; token_check for price plus safety warnings; crypto_market_pulse for BTC, ETH and SOL at once. Parameters: token: ERC-20 contract or SPL mint ("SOL" works on Solana). chain: base (default), ethereum or solana. Returns: price_usd, the pool used, its liquidity, and a thin_liquidity flag when the price shouldn't be trusted.

+When to use: You have a transaction hash and need to know if it went through and what moved. Parameters: hash: 0x hash on Base or Ethereum, base58 signature on Solana. chain: base (default), ethereum or solana; it must match the hash. Returns: status, time, sender, fee, and every token transfer with symbol and amount (on Solana, balance changes per owner).
+When to use: Before paying, to see exactly what get_product_details returns. Use instead: get_product_details for a URL you choose. Returns: a real extraction of one fixed sample page.

+When to use: Someone handed you an attestation, or you want to check one of yours. Parameters: attestation: the full attest_page response or just its attestation object, as JSON text. Returns: whether the signature is valid and whether this service issued it, with the reasons.

+When to use: You need what a wallet holds, in token amounts. Use instead: wallet_portfolio for USD values and a total; check_my_balance (free) for your own USDC on Base. Parameters: address is required. chain: base (default), ethereum or solana; the address format must match. tokens: up to 20 extra ERC-20 contracts or SPL mints to include. Returns: native coin, USDC (USDT on Ethereum and Solana) and the tokens you listed, each with symbol, decimals and amount.

+When to use: You need a wallet's value in USD: each holding priced and the total. Use instead: wallet_balance when amounts are enough (cheaper). Parameters: address is required. chain: base (default), ethereum or solana. tokens: up to 20 extra contracts or mints to include. Returns: holdings[] with amount, USD price, USD value and pool used, the total in USD, and warnings for thin pools or positions bigger than their pool.
